1.title: GERMAN LESSON 1: Learn German for Beginners – German Greetings
1.focus: Watch once, then again while repeating each greeting aloud. Notice which greeting belongs to which time of day and which goodbye is formal.

questions.q: Anja says one goodbye is formal, for people you do not know very well. Which one?
questions.why: Auf Wiedersehen is the formal goodbye; Tschüss is for friends and family.

questions.q: Anja points out a pattern: “Guten Morgen, Guten Tag, Guten Abend” but “Gute Nacht”. Why?
o: Nacht is feminine; Morgen, Tag and Abend are masculine
Gute Nacht is only used in the south
questions.why: Masculine nouns take “Guten” (accusative), the feminine noun die Nacht takes “Gute”.

questions.q: Anja’s informal question for friends: “Hallo! Wie geht es ___?”
questions.why: Wie geht es dir? is the informal way to ask how someone is.

2.title: GERMAN PRONUNCIATION 1: The German Alphabet
2.focus: Say every letter out loud with Anja. Then spell your own first name and last name, exactly as she asks at the end.

questions.q: What homework does Anja give at the end of the video?
o: Spell your first and last name in German
Write a short email to a friend
questions.why: She asks you to learn the letters and spell your first and last name.

questions.q: Which German city does Anja spell in her exercise, after spelling her own name?
questions.why: She spells Berlin, the capital of Germany: B – E – R – L – I – N.

questions.q: For the letter E, what does Anja tell you to do with your mouth?
o: Pull it apart wide, like a smile
Round your lips into a circle
questions.why: The German E needs your mouth pulled apart.
